articles.title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war amid surge in Russian recruitment
articles.summary:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort

Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation.

The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.

articles.title: Trump could be about to sell out Ukraine. Europe must get its act together, fast | Paul Taylor
articles.summary:
A deal giving Moscow a slice of Ukrainian territory and sanctions relief could be on the table in weeks – yet European leaders are busy squabbling

Donald Trump has lost substantial power over domestic policy after last week’s devastating midterm losses, but his ability to cement his legacy by upending US foreign policy remains largely intact.

There is every reason to fear a ”great betrayal” of Ukraine in the coming weeks, one that would reward Vladimir Putin for Russia’s war of aggression against Kyiv, and also do lasting damage to the European security order. Yet lilliputian European leaders are too busy squabbling over who should represent them in future peace talks to focus on how to prevent a sellout. Despite fundamental European interests being at stake in this week’s three-way US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Europe is relegated to a side room, represented by a posse of officials from the UK, France, Germany, the EU and Nato.

articles.title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
articles.summary:
Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit

Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.

“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”

The COP31 climate summit in Antalya highlights the impact of rising populism on EU green policies, while macroeconomic conditions are shaped by stable inflation trends and wage pressures monitored by the ECB.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to react to the outcomes of diplomatic negotiations in Abu Dhabi and incoming macroeconomic releases.

archive.security_status_cs: V Abú Dhabí probíhají první významná mírová jednání o Ukrajině za účasti USA, Ruska a Ukrajiny, doprovázená však pokračujícími útoky. Evropské bezpečnostní struktury čelí rostoucím hrozbám v podobě kybernetických útoků na infrastrukturu (např. francouzské mrazírenské systémy připisované Íránu) a vnitřních politických napětí. Italské banky zároveň protestují proti novému vládnímu daňovému zatížení a ECB sleduje stabilizující se inflační a mzdové trendy.
archive.security_status_en: Substantive peace talks on Ukraine are underway in Abu Dhabi with US, Russian, and Ukrainian participation, though overshadowed by ongoing strikes. European security faces escalating threats from critical infrastructure cyberattacks—such as the Iranian-linked hacking of French refrigeration systems—and domestic political tensions. Simultaneously, Italian banks are pushing back against new government tax raids while the ECB monitors stabilizing inflation and wage metrics.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to react to any progress or stagnation in the Abu Dhabi peace talks alongside inflation pressures in the US and Europe.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí stupňujícím se geopolitickým tlakům kvůli probíhajícím mírovým jednáním o Ukrajině v Abú Dhabí a obavám z možného amerického posunu pod tlakem administrativy USA. Ekonomické prostředí zatěžují rostoucí inflační tlaky na mzdy, energetická nestabilita a sílící protekcionistická opatření vůči čínskému dovozu.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces escalating geopolitical pressures amid ongoing Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi and concerns over a potential US policy shift under pressure. archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává, že trhy budou reagovat především na výstupy z trilateralních mírových rozhovorů v Abú Dhabí a na napětí kolem námořních hranic ve Středozemním moři.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to react primarily to the outcomes of trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi and tensions over Mediterranean maritime borders.
